Description
I was reading through studentregsanity.py and noticed a variable scoping issue in the sanitize_walkin function. The loop that actually expires the registrations (for sr in srs:) is sitting outside the section loop. Because of this, it only ever processes the very last section.

Steps to Reproduce
Since this is a backend logic bug, here is how to spot it in the code:

Open esp/esp/program/controllers/studentregsanity.py.

Scroll to the sanitize_walkin function.

Notice that the for sr in srs: block is outdented too far—it runs after the for sec in w.get_sections(): loop is completely finished.

If this runs on a program with multiple walk-in sections, earlier sections are completely skipped. Also, if there are 0 sections, the script will crash with an UnboundLocalError since srs is never assigned.

Expected Behavior
The code should iterate through all sections and expire the walk-in registrations for every single section. (The sanitize_lunch function right below it handles this nesting correctly).

Actual Behavior
It only cleans up the last section because the cleanup loop just uses the leftover srs variable from the finished section loop.

Screenshots
No response

Operating System
No response

Browser
No response

Additional Context
The fix is pretty straightforward—just indent the for sr in srs: block and the report.append line so they sit inside the for sec... loop. I would like to work on this issue
input.prText:
Description
This PR fixes the scoping bug in sanitize_walkin where it was skipping earlier walk-in sections and only expiring registrations for the very last one.

I fixed the indentation so the registration cleanup loop is properly nested inside the section loop. While I was in there, I also made a tiny optimization: I moved the if not fake: check outside the for sr in srs: loop so it only evaluates once per section instead of redundantly for every single student registration.

Related Issue
Closes #5460

- **Codecov Guardrails:** Switching patch coverage from `no` to a `60%` target actively prevents new PRs from introducing untested lines.
- **Actionable Documentation:** The testing guide addresses tricky, ESP-specific test behavior (e.g., `@needs_admin` returning 200 with an error template instead of 403).

## Potential Issues / Risks
- **CI Friction on Small PRs:** A strictly enforced 60% patch target may cause CI failures on small refactors or multi-line bug fixes that touch mostly uncovered edge cases.

## Suggestions / Improvements
- **Local Coverage Workflow:** Include a quick snippet in `docs/dev/testing.rst` explaining how to run pytest with local coverage flags (`pytest --cov=esp`) so authors can verify patch coverage before pushing.
